title: The manager-scope guard's identity source was archived, so it reported PASS on a manager doing items — plus three cost leaks
note:
[!] THE E20 LANE HAS STOPPED — NOBODY IS WORKING THIS ROW. Work complete in two PRs, BOTH MERGE-PENDING with auto-merge armed: #12740 (the guard's identity + fail-closed + the planted 2026-09-21 regression) and #12742 (the three cost causes, the reconciler, the manager SKILL.md controls). `lane` is deliberately null rather than still naming the session: lane_reconcile.py's own `in_flight with NO lane` check now fires on this row, which is the correct alarm. MOVE THIS TO `landed_unproven` WHEN BOTH MERGE, and to `done` on the observation named at the end of this note. === WHAT WAS DELIVERED. (A) THE ROOT CAUSE, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THE THREE COST LEAKS: scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py derived manager identity only from MANAGER-LEASE.json, which the 2026-09-21 reset ARCHIVED, so the roster froze at 7 sessions (last run ending 2026-09-19T10:42:44Z) and could never grow. RE-VERIFIED every line rather than trusting the dispatch. MEASURED FURTHER: that day's manager has 38 commits, 31 off MANAGER_SURFACE (config/accounts.yaml x6, tests x5, scripts/ops x4, src/web/api/routers/work.py x2, scripts/ci x1), every one graded `not_manager` and skipped. FIXED: identity is now the UNION of derived sources; new `dispatch` source = a commit newly setting a row's `lane` to a session OTHER than its own. MEASURED over 635 commits: 12 dispatch acts, 1 session named, FALSE POSITIVES 0 of 1, the 6 self-lane-only sessions NOT admitted, FALSE NEGATIVES 7 of 7 vs the lease and STRUCTURAL (pre-reset `lane` held a team name: engineering 30, ops 29, research 18, zero session ids) which is why both sources stay. INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by a surface I did not use: list_sessions' own `parent_session_id` names exactly 2 managers across 58 lanes — that day's (found by dispatch) and session_01GHpyXT2qssLJsrvXBQRkQF (found by the lease). The union covers both. (B) IT FAILS CLOSED, which matters more: no live identity source -> `no_identity_source`, live source with an empty roster -> `identity_unresolved`, BOTH FAIL at EXIT 2 (distinct from 1 for a real finding). It previously returned 7 stale ids and carried on. (C) THE REGRESSION IS PLANTED: --self-test 33 -> 40 cases. (D) THE TRAP WAS NOT WALKED INTO: 18 of the 38 still FAIL R2 after the change. Two paths were admitted, each the moved subject of an already-argued rule: .github/merge-slots/** graded PER COMMIT (own branch only), and research/queue/** as the surviving half of the 2026-09-03 operator ruling that filing is management. (E) THE THREE COST CAUSES, MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-22T13:02Z over the 60 most recent sessions, $5,892.69 readable of 51 of 60: 14 lanes over ceiling (B1 12.4x, not the six this row said — the row read running totals, its own cause 1); 22 finished-but-unarchived sessions holding $2,088.73; 4 BLOCKED lanes holding $1,347.60. [!] THE HEADLINE AND IT IS 30x THIS ROW'S ESTIMATE: session_01XYu2vvg9Qgxoqf4jJQyd8i (ENGINEERING LANE MI-305, spawned by the PREVIOUS manager 2026-09-18) has sat BLOCKED and IDLE 72.8 hours holding $1,343.06 and has NEVER COMMITTED A LINE — more than this row's entire 13-lane day in one session that produced nothing. Filed as PI-20260922-ONE-BLOCKED-LANE-HAS-HELD-1343-USD-FOR-72-HOURS-HAVING-NEVER-COMMITTED-A-LINE-AND-22-FINISHED-LANES-SIT-UNARCHIVED. A walled lane needs a HUMAN to clear its prompt and archiving another manager's lanes is the MANAGER's call, so it is surfaced, not cleared. (F) THE INVOLUNTARY MECHANISM IS BUILT, TRIED AND HONESTLY NOT WORKING. Two cheaper designs were KILLED ON MEASUREMENT first: a CI guard on git commit recency (5 of 7 WORKING lanes had NEVER committed, so it would have redded five healthy lanes) and a CI guard on the offline half (it would fail contributors for the manager's behaviour). The chosen design — a Routine firing a FRESH session, so the manager is not in the path — was created, FIRED ONCE, and DISABLED the same minute: the fired session has no repo checkout and no MCP connectors, so it can neither run the script nor call list_sessions. THE INVARIANT IS THEREFORE STILL VOLUNTARY and says so; what stands is a DISCIPLINE in SKILL.md, labelled as one. Filed as PI-20260922-THE-LANE-WATCHDOG-ROUTINE-FIRES-SESSIONS-WITH-NO-REPO-AND-NO-MCP-SO-IT-IS-DISABLED-AND-THE-INVARIANT-IS-STILL-VOLUNTARY — the operator must attach the connector + source in the Routines UI, which a session cannot do. (G) ALSO FILED, found while fixing R2 and not walked past: R6/R7/R8's subjects are ALL absent on main too, so three of four rules grade nothing and two did it silently — PI-20260922-MANAGER-SCOPE-R6-R7-R8-HAVE-NO-SUBJECT-AFTER-THE-RESET-SO-THREE-OF-FOUR-RULES-GRADE-NOTHING. === REACHED: MERGED is not yet true (both PRs armed, not merged). DEPLOYED and OBSERVED are not claimed for anything in this row. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: check_manager_scope.py printing `identity source `dispatch`: live` with the current manager on the roster, AND a `violation` on a real PR graded from main rather than from a branch. === WHAT THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL TEXT GOT WRONG, kept so it is not re-quoted: 'six lanes exceeded theirs' is 14 when measured after archiving, and 'final spends read off get_session' is only true via external_metadata.usage.cost_usd, which is ABSENT on 9 of 60 sessions — 6 of them WORKING — so an unreadable cost must render as could-not-look, never $0. === ORIGINAL ROW TEXT FOLLOWS === MEASURED 2026-09-21 across 12 dispatched lanes, final spends read off get_session: roughly $860 against ceilings totalling ~$250. Six lanes exceeded theirs; two exceeded by more than 6x (B1 $270.39/$35, B2 $229.13/$30). [!] THREE DISTINCT CAUSES, and they need different fixes -- lumping them as 'lanes are expensive' would fix none. (1) A CEILING NOBODY CHECKS MID-FLIGHT IS NOT A CEILING. Nothing reads spend during a run; the manager set ceilings and looked once, at the end. A1's meter now exists and this is its first real consumer. (2) FINISHED LANES KEEP SPENDING. A9 went $37.13 -> $50.78 AFTER its work merged, sitting subscribed to its own PR; E16 went $25.38 -> $56.14 the same way. Watching a PR is not free and the lane has nothing left to contribute to it. Archive on merge, or do not subscribe a lane to the PR the manager is going to merge anyway. (3) AN UNATTENDED LANE CAN HIT AN INTERACTIVE PERMISSION PROMPT AND SPEND ITS WHOLE BUDGET THERE. B2 did, twice. The second attempt's pending action was readable and specific: a COMPOUND, PIPED git command (`git fetch ... 2>&1 | tail -5 && git merge ... 2>&1 | tail -60`) awaiting a Bash approval nobody was present to give. ⚠️ THAT COMMAND SHAPE IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT ESTABLISHED -- other lanes committed and pushed all day, so it is not universal. Establish WHICH shapes are refused before writing a rule about it; a dispatch instruction based on a guess would be the same category of error this repo keeps paying for. [!] THE CHEAPEST FIX IS PROBABLY (2) AND IT IS FREE: stop subscribing lanes to PRs the manager merges. [!] ⚠️ THE TOTAL ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, AND THE ERROR WAS THIS ROW'S OWN CAUSE (1). It said ~$860. Read again after every lane was ARCHIVED, the total is ~$1,142 across 13 lanes. B1 alone is $435.05, not the $270.39 committed a few hours earlier -- it accrued $165 MORE while IDLE, watching the PR the manager was about to merge anyway. A1 is $59.17, not $28.03. [!] SO THE MANAGER MADE THE SAME MISTAKE TWICE IN ONE DAY, the second time inside the commit describing the mistake. The mechanism is exact and unglamorous: get_session on a LIVE lane returns a RUNNING total, and a running total written onto a row reads like a final one. [!] THE RULE IS MECHANICAL, NOT 'be more careful': A LANE'S SPEND IS FINAL ONLY ONCE THE LANE IS ARCHIVED. Read it there, or record it with the read-time and the word `running` beside it. A number with no read-time is the same defect as a count that cannot say whether anyone looked. [!] AND IT SHARPENS CAUSE (2) from 'lanes keep spending' into a SIZE: the idle-watching tail is the single largest line in the day's spend, larger than any lane's actual work. [!] AND ONE MORE INSTANCE, CAUGHT IN THE ACT WHILE WRITING THIS ROW: resolving the checklist conflict with a 'longest note wins' heuristic silently reverted B1's state from `done` to `in_flight`. A heuristic that cannot say WHY it chose a side is the same defect as a count that cannot say whether anyone looked. States are now set explicitly from the merges performed, and the heuristic is not reused.  === E20 LANE UPDATE 2026-09-22 (session_011xpvJ2MQgd4jmKkdfg6gzV, branch claude/e20-manager-identity-fail-closed). THE ROOT CAUSE IS BIGGER THAN THE THREE COST LEAKS AND IS FIXED FIRST. RE-VERIFIED EVERY LINE rather than taken from the dispatch: lease_holders() -> 7 sessions across 478 revisions of MANAGER-LEASE.json, every lease-holding run ending 2026-09-19T10:42:44Z; MANAGER-LEASE.json ABSENT on origin/main (archived by the reset); session_01XQhayAHWdrSYv8jN54P2HH NOT on the roster. MEASURED FURTHER, which the dispatch did not state: that session has 38 commits and 31 touch a path off MANAGER_SURFACE -- config/accounts.yaml x6, tests/** x5, scripts/ops/** x4, src/web/api/routers/work.py x2, scripts/ci/** x1 -- and every one graded `not_manager` and was skipped. [!] IDENTITY IS NOW A UNION OF DERIVED SOURCES. New source `dispatch`: a commit that newly sets a row's `lane` to a session OTHER than its own trailer's. MEASURED over 635 commits touching this file: 12 dispatch acts naming 1 session -- that day's manager. FALSE POSITIVES 0 of 1. The 6 sessions that set a lane only to THEMSELVES are NOT admitted, which is the over-capture `updated_by` would have produced. FALSE NEGATIVES 7 of 7 against the lease roster, and STRUCTURAL not a flaw: pre-reset `lane` held a TEAM NAME (engineering 30, ops 29, research 18, zero session ids), so the signal did not exist before 2026-09-21 -- hence the union, in which a retired source keeps contributing history and simply cannot grow. [!] AND THE HALF THAT MATTERS MORE: IT FAILS CLOSED. Each source declares the path whose presence at HEAD decides whether it can grow (live/retired/unreadable, never collapsed). No live source -> `no_identity_source`; live source with an empty roster -> `identity_unresolved`. BOTH FAIL AT EXIT 2, distinct from exit 1 for a real finding, per the canonical doc's `could not measure is its own outcome`. Previously an empty roster returned 7 stale ids and carried on, or state `unattributed` and exit 0. [!] THE 2026-09-21 REGRESSION IS PLANTED: --self-test goes 33 -> 40 cases, including `lease archived + manager identified only by dispatch -> violation` (without the second source it is `no_manager_commits`, a pass) and `every subject removed -> exit 2`. `exit_code` is a function so the test asserts the exit code instead of the docstring claiming it. [!] REPORTED, NOT WALKED PAST: R6/R7/R8 have no subject either -- SESSIONS.json, MERGE-QUEUE.json and the lease are all absent on main, so three of four rules grade NOTHING and two did it silently. Every run now prints a RULE LIVENESS block. Filed as PI-20260922-MANAGER-SCOPE-R6-R7-R8-HAVE-NO-SUBJECT-AFTER-THE-RESET-SO-THREE-OF-FOUR-RULES-GRADE-NOTHING with a rerun; retiring vs re-pointing them is an operator decision, not this lane's. [!] THE TRAP WAS NOT WALKED INTO: MANAGER_SURFACE is not widened until the manager's commits pass. AFTER this change 18 of the 38 still FAIL R2 (4 more are under active dated exceptions, 7 are per-branch merge-slot claims, 7 were already on the surface). Two paths were admitted, each as the moved subject of an already-argued rule and neither wholesale: .github/merge-slots/** graded PER COMMIT by branch_slot_claim_only (own branch only), the successor of the session-board merge_slot carve-out the same reset archived; and research/queue/** as the surviving half of the 2026-09-03 OPERATOR RULING that filing is management, whose named file (health-review-backlog.json) the reset also archived. [!] (4) AND (5) ARE DELIVERED in #12742, not outstanding: the three cost causes measured live, the reconciler extended with fmt_cost refusing a bare spend figure, and the manager SKILL.md controls. [!] PLUS A FOURTH THING THE MANAGER HANDED THIS LANE MID-SESSION, because it is the same defect class: check_manager_queue_watch reporting NEVER_RAN_OVERDUE after 479 hours and zero receipts. ROOT-CAUSED AT THE PRIMARY SOURCE and it is the SAME cause as this lane's own failed watchdog — a Routine-fired session gets NO repo checkout and NO mcp__ connectors, so that Routine could never perform either half of its own prompt, while firing hourly and reporting SUCCEEDED (~479 firings, roughly $90). Two independent Routines, same two absences, with the negative control run (an ordinary lane DOES return session_context.sources). DISPOSITION: do NOT retire the guard — it is the only thing that noticed; the decision is about the ROUTINES and only the operator can grant what they need. [!] AND THE SWEEP THE MANAGER ASKED FOR, with its population: 95 guard scripts, every module-level repo-path constant tested against HEAD. FOUR STATES: 46 no_declared_subject (the instrument cannot speak to them, counted separately and never folded into live), 30 live, 11 DEGRADED, 8 DEAD — grading nothing. All 19 are the 2026-09-21 reset's blast radius, and THREE OF THE DEAD (check_claim_basis, check_soak_registered, check_operator_owed) are named in docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md as LIVE MECHANISMS. The naive probe was measured and KILLED first (29 of 69, dominated by self-test fixtures). Mechanism: scripts/ci/check_guard_liveness.py, WIRED into run_guards.py, report-first with a shrink-only baseline so it does not red-wall the repo on day one. [!] AND THE STRUCTURAL HALF, built after the manager supplied the design constraint that FRESHNESS BELONGS IN CI RATHER THAN ON A TIMER — because the obvious fix (emit receipts, grade their freshness) IS check_manager_queue_watch, i.e. instance #3, so a scheduled grader can always be the thing that did not fire while CI's own liveness is proven by PRs merging at all. scripts/ci/check_cadence_liveness.py, WIRED as `cadence-liveness`, DERIVES its population from the tree (workflow `schedule:` crons + deploy/*.timer OnCalendar) and FAILS on anything derived-but-unregistered, so omission is detectable rather than a hand-maintained list. MEASURED: 38 in-repo cadence declarations, of which fresh 1 / no_receipt 37 / unregistered 0 — EXACTLY ONE OF THIRTY-EIGHT SCHEDULED THINGS CAN CURRENTLY BE SEEN TO HAVE RUN. The 37 split into 8 that already commit back (one declared output path from gradeable, the cheap shrink) and 29 with no in-repo trace at all. [!] RESIDUAL NAMED IN A DISCLOSURE PRINTED ON EVERY RUN: a ROUTINE is not derivable from the repo, so a Routine's omission is NOT detected — and instance #3 was a Routine. Both halves of this class bottom out in the SAME operator action: attach the connector and a source to the Routines, or delete them. [!] OBSERVED 2026-09-22T14:35Z, AND THIS IS THE THING THE ROW HANGS ON — not the merge. #12740 merged as 76a58117; the guard was then run FROM MAIN against a real branch (the first attempt ran the BRANCH's copy, which predated the merge and printed the old output — recorded because it is the same 'wrong version' error the row is about). Main's version reports: identity source `dispatch` (MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json) **live**, contributing 1 session — the current manager; identity source `lease` **retired**, contributing 7; manager roster = UNION of both = **8 sessions**, where before the fix it was frozen at 7 and structurally unable to grow; and **5 manager commits graded, all inside the surface**, where the same commits previously graded `not_manager` and were skipped entirely. The RULE LIVENESS block prints and names R6, R7 and R8 as DEAD — subject absent at HEAD — rather than passing in silence. That is E20's stated closing condition met verbatim: 'a `live` dispatch source with the current manager on the roster, on a real PR graded from main'. [!] STILL OPEN on this row: #12742 (the reconciler, the three cost causes and the guard-liveness sweep) is pushed, conflict-resolved against main and waiting on CI. The row is NOT done until it lands. And R6/R7/R8 having no subject is a SEPARATE disposition, now carried by row E45 under the operator's re-point-three/retire-the-rest decision.

[!] WITHDRAWN 2026-09-24 — THE 'ONLY A HUMAN CAN CLEAR IT' CLAIM ABOVE IS FALSE AND WAS NEVER TESTED. It is left in place rather than deleted so the correction is legible against what it corrects. FALSIFIED by one attempt: interrupt_session on the walled lane, then a message delivered through a create_trigger with persistent_session_id set to it. MEASURED on session_017mdYduTwtyVPXU54wqNHJx, which had shown no activity for 39 hours (last 2026-09-22T13:51:41Z): the trigger fired 2026-09-24T05:32:00Z and get_session shows a turn at 05:32:42Z ending status_bucket COMPLETED, reporting a clean tree, nothing staged or unpushed, and that its own staged_files:true flag was a FALSE ALARM. The operator's words, recorded because the correction is theirs: 'you can definitely take care of those permissions instead of me'.
[!] AND THE NARROWER FORM, because over-claiming the correction would repeat the original error in the other direction: ONE case establishes this, not two. The same technique was also aimed at session_01R9WFrBK1sbBcpTYgBmvG1q and it did reply, but that session runs a 6-hourly cron that would have woken it anyway, and its own 06:44Z heartbeat states it 'was not itself blocked on anything at the time'. A session that was going to wake regardless is not evidence that a message clears a wall. What is established: a message CAN move a session reporting BLOCKED. What is NOT established: that it always can, or what distinguishes the cases. Do not read this as a guarantee; read it as a probe that must be RUN rather than assumed either way — the original defect was asserting the limit for two days without ever attempting it once. DONE — VERIFIED 2026-09-25 by running scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py --base origin/main~300 against origin/main HEAD myself: identity source `dispatch` live, contributing 3 sessions incl. the current manager (session_01Ljhs6sFAdWHdMDhJpL5aBP), which is graded (R2 violations named) rather than skipped; manager roster (union of live+retired sources) = 10; --self-test 40/40. Both #12740 and #12742 confirmed merged ancestors of origin/main via merge-base. Closing condition met verbatim.
